items.action: Update every WordPress install to 7.1.2 (or the matching backport for your branch) immediately and confirm the running version — do not assume auto-updates applied.
items.details: Affected: every release from 4.7.0 through 7.1.1; fixed in 7.1.2 with backports to 13 older branches down to 4.7. Remote code execution requires a theme with a top-level directory starting with "page-" and a readable local PHP file such as pearcmd.php, but probing is indiscriminate.
items.summary: Attackers started exploiting CVE-2026-87902, an unauthenticated path-traversal flaw in WordPress Core's page-template resolution, within hours of the Sept 22 patch. Patchstack saw the first probe at 11:49 UTC that day; activity has since escalated 10x, with attackers including pearcmd.php and writing PHP web shells to disk.
items.title: Attackers exploit critical WordPress flaw CVE-2026-87902 within hours of patch

items.action: Upgrade self-hosted Dokploy instances to 0.29.13 or later; audit org-member activity for unexpected shell command execution.
items.details: The patch.readRepoDirectories tRPC procedure passes the user-controlled repoPath into child_process.exec as root in the Dokploy container. Standard deployments mount /var/run/docker.sock, so container-root execution can escalate to full Docker host compromise.
items.summary: CVE-2026-93425 (CVSS 9.9) is an OS command-injection flaw in Dokploy disclosed Sept 24: an authenticated org member with service:read permission can inject shell metacharacters into repoPath and execute arbitrary commands as root. A public proof-of-concept is already circulating.
items.title: Dokploy CVE-2026-93425: critical command injection with public PoC

items.action: Update to sudo 1.9.17-16.p2.2.hum1, and append a trailing 'Z' to all time-restricted sudoers rules as the recommended mitigation.
items.details: The flaw only affects systems using optional notbefore/notafter time-based sudoers rules. No active exploitation or public PoC is confirmed; PAM authentication remains intact, so attackers cannot exceed what their original rule grants.
items.summary: CVE-2026-96512 (CVSS 7.8) lets local users bypass sudo's time-based authorization by manipulating the tz environment variable, defeating notbefore/notafter restrictions in sudoers rules.
items.title: Sudo timezone flaw CVE-2026-96512 bypasses time-based sudoers restrictions

items.details: The $351.6M figure comes from CEO Gracy Chen; Arkham's Emmett Gallic flagged initial hot-wallet movements (~$178M) earlier, with more moving afterward. The breach was contained to hot/warm wallet layers; cold wallets remain secure and a $464M+ user protection fund backs user balances.
items.summary: Crypto exchange Bitget confirmed Sept 24 that unauthorized transfers drained about $351.6M from hot and warm wallets; withdrawals are suspended pending a security review. CEO Gracy Chen says preliminary IP/VPN clues point to North Korean actors, and some stolen funds have reportedly been recovered.
items.title: Bitget loses ~$352M in hot-wallet breach; suspects North Korea

items.details: FBIJobs.gov displayed a "seized by ShinyHunters" banner before returning 503 errors; the bureau has not confirmed whether the intrusion hit its own systems or a third-party provider supporting the portal.
items.summary: The FBI is actively investigating ShinyHunters' claim of stealing 2–3 terabytes of data from its online jobs system, including a sample spreadsheet with thousands of current/former employees' PII and details of sensitive intelligence assignments. The breach point is still undetermined.
items.title: FBI probes ShinyHunters' claim of massive jobs-portal data theft

items.details: As with all leak-site listings, these are unconfirmed allegations — disclosure on a leak site does not prove the scale or success of the underlying intrusion.
items.summary: New Sept 24 dark-web leak-site disclosures include Qilin naming All Tech Machine & Engineering (US manufacturing), Akira naming Wallatec, Rhysida naming NEAD Pro, Spirals naming Armada Credit Bureau (Uganda financial services), and Krybit naming jonesthegrocer.com.
items.title: Fresh ransomware leak-site claims: Qilin, Akira, Rhysida and others name new victims

items.details: FLATROOF and ROOFDECK were previously seen in the March–April 2026 attack on KelpDAO's LayerZero bridge. The campaign uses fake GitHub coding-project repos and job-interview lures aimed at DevOps, crypto, and fintech staff.
items.summary: SentinelOne attributed the compromise of an India-based IT services firm to North Korea's Jade Sleet (aka TraderTraitor/UNC4899), which deployed the Apple macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK. Reported Sept 21; the group typically targets crypto-adjacent firms through developer-focused social engineering.
items.title: North Korea's Jade Sleet linked to breach of Indian IT provider
